subject: Deployment pathways review — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Air-gapped private
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@lumothera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — deployment options and immediate asks

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps as you evaluate Hosted API vs Dedicated vs a fully air-gapped Private deployment: 

Summary of your needs (as discussed):
- Primary: strong data residency and audit controls for clinical research workloads (PII/PHI)
- Secondary: deterministic latency for batch inference during overnight analysis windows
- Constraint: site is currently air-gapped for research environment B (no outbound internet) but you do have an on-prem analytics cluster in environment A that can connect to vendor-hosted APIs

Key trade-offs we covered:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, lowest operational burden, but requires transmitting data out of your air-gapped environment (acceptable for environment A, not B)
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated): reserved GPU pools in our private tenancy — good for predictable throughput and stricter isolation, still requires egress unless coupled with Private connectivity options
- Private (VPC / on-prem appliance): supports offline / air-gapped operations and KMS/HSM integration for keys — requires hardware footprint onsite and a maintenance cadence for offline upgrades

Immediate asks / action items (who / when):
1) Claire: send the server inventory for environment B (OS, NICs, storage, available racks, power/cooling) so our infra team can confirm compatibility. If possible please include the file we discussed (CSV or XLSX). [Attachment stub accepted] — by EOD Wed 8/25
2) Redwood (Ben/Neha): provide a conservative HW compatibility matrix and an initial checklist of offline upgrade steps + expected downtime for appliance updates — by Thu 8/26
3) Rachel: schedule a 60-min on-site scoping call w/ your facilities + network team (we’ll propose dates after we review inventory) — will send Doodle today

Attachments I’m including: redwood-private-checklist.pdf (high-level checklist) and a sample onprem-hw-specs.xlsx (for your ops team to fill).

If the inventory for env B confirms that there are no virtualization constraints and you can host two 4U nodes, a minimal on-prem demo is feasible in ~6 weeks from hardware availability. If racks/power are limited, we’ll lean on a hybrid approach (Dedicated for burst + Private for sensitive workloads).

Thanks — please reply right into this thread with the inventory file or any clarifying constraints.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

[Attachment: onprem-hw-specs.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@lumothera.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment options and immediate asks

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the inventory export for environment B and a short note from our facilities lead on power limits. Environment B is air-gapped; there is a small concierge team that can accept physical media for updates but no network egress is permitted from the cluster itself.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- Inventory attached: lumothera-server-inventory.csv — includes OS, NIC speeds (1Gb/10Gb), available rack units, and whether each host is virtualized
- We have two spare 2U bays in Rack 7 but only 1 available 1200W PDUs leg per rack — if more than two nodes are required we’ll need a facilities change request.
- Security requires that any software updates be provided as signed artifacts and applied via offline media by our engineering ops team. We will not accept direct SSH from vendor engineers.

Next for you: can Redwood provide the offline upgrade flow (checksum/signature verification) and an estimate of how long an appliance update would take (including time for staging signed packages)? Also — any option to run inference on site against pre-trained, quantized artifacts without frequent updates? That would reduce cadence.

Attaching lumothera-server-inventory.csv and a short facilities note (included in the CSV metadata).

—Claire
Claire Zhang
Head of Data Engineering, LumoThera
claire.zhang@lumothera.com

[Attachment: lumothera-server-inventory.csv (csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@lumothera.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment options and immediate asks

Claire — appreciate the inventory. Quick read and initial responses: 

1) Compatibility: based on the NIC and rack info, we can fit a minimal two-node on-prem appliance in Rack 7 (two 2U nodes). Power is tight: we recommend planning for either a second PDU leg or a single higher-wattage node (4U) to consolidate. I’ll flag Marissa to confirm exact current appliance draw.

2) Offline upgrade flow: Redwood supports signed, tarball-based offline updates. Typical steps:
- We produce a signed artifact (SHA256 + vendor signature) and a human-readable manifest
- You retrieve artifact via a secure transfer channel your procurement team chooses (SFTP or physical media)
- Your ops team verifies signature and applies update using our offline apply script
- We provide a validation checklist and rollback artifact as part of the package

Estimated durations (conservative):
- Staging & validation of the artifact on the appliance: 15–30 minutes
- Applying the update (minor kernel/service restart): 10–20 minutes
- Post-update validation and regression smoke tests: 30–45 minutes
Total window: ~1–1.5 hours for a minor release. Major model/format changes (re-quantization, significant runtime upgrades) could take 2–4 hours including offline model upload and cache warm-up.

3) Cadence reduction: yes — we can provide a quantized model bundle that is designed for longer-term offline stability. That approach minimizes runtime patches; you would only need model bundle updates when performance/accuracy regressions are unacceptable.

Action proposal (mutual action plan):
- Thu 8/26: Redwood to send full HW compatibility matrix + sample offline artifact package (Rachel/Marissa)
- Mon 8/30: 60-min scoping call with your facilities + network + security to confirm PDU and transport process (Rachel to set)
- By Fri 9/10: target pilot deploy window (onsite hardware & offline artifact staging)

I’m copying Marissa (ops) to start the compatibility confirmation. Claire, if you want we can also propose a hybrid alternative (Dedicated for non-sensitive batch jobs + on-prem for env B) to get you immediate throughput while we validate the offline appliance.

–Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@lumothera.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment options and immediate asks

Claire — thanks for the quick response and inventory. Confirming and next steps here so procurement/facilities have a single source of truth: 

Confirmed from Redwood:
- We can support an air-gapped private deployment in env B with signed offline artifacts and a one-hour minor-update maintenance window.
- If you want reduced cadence, we’ll deliver a quantized model bundle for the pilot and treat runtime changes as a separate program with scheduled rollouts.

Concrete next steps (owners / dates):
1) Rachel: Doodle for scoping call Tues 8/31–Fri 9/3 (facilities + network + security) — invite will go out today
2) Ben/Marissa: deliver the full HW compatibility matrix and estimated power draw for 2U vs 4U configs — by Thu 8/26 EOD (attached)
3) Claire/Procurement: confirm whether LumoThera will accept physical media for updates or requires an SFTP transfer record for auditing — reply to this thread by Mon 8/30
4) All: target pilot window of 9/13–9/17 (contingent on hardware availability) — we’ll firm this up after the scoping call

Attached: redwood-private-checklist.pdf (updated) and a condensed onprem-hw-specs.xlsx with our recommended footprint. If facilities can free a second PDU leg we’ll aim for two 2U nodes; otherwise we’ll discuss a single 4U consolidated node for the pilot.

Thanks — we’ll treat the hybrid Dedicated + Private plan as our contingency and outline cost estimates in the next note once hardware direction is chosen.

—Rachel
